transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because... I just know the people living at my apartment are watching me. They keep track of my comings and goings, and they're slipping notes about me down to the main office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just, you know, regular notices they put on the doors, but I know what they're really doing.
Have you been hearing any voices or sounds that other people do not seem to hear?
No, I haven't heard anything like that. Just the usual sounds around the building, nothing out of the ordinary. No voices or anything that other people aren't hearing.
How long have you been feeling that your neighbors are monitoring you like this?
Well, let's see... it's been going on for a while. I'd say it's been right about a year and a month now that I've been noticing what they're doing, the neighbors and the office, I mean.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, organize your thoughts, or follow through with your daily tasks since this started?

Yeah, I have noticed that. It's gotten pretty hard to keep up with my daily stuff. Like, my bills and appointment cards just pile up on the table. I'll sit down and try to go through them, but I just end up reading the same line again and again... and I still can't decide what needs doing first. My mind just doesn't want to sort it out.
Have you found it harder to experience pleasure in the things you used to enjoy, or have you felt less motivated to talk to or interact with other people lately?

Yeah, it's definitely gotten harder. I used to really look forward to things... like choir practice, playing bridge, or even just cooking a pot of beans on Sunday. I used to like doing little repair jobs for folks, too. But now... I mostly just let the phone ring. I just tell myself there is no point in going or doing any of it.
When you are speaking to others, do they ever tell you that your sentences are difficult to follow or that what you are saying does not seem to make sense?

Yeah, people do tell me that. Or they just give me this confused look. Like, when I try to explain things, I'll start off talking about the rent... and then I'll move on to the marina, then the choir robes, and then the wires in the walls. And people just look at me like I skipped half the story. It makes sense to me when I'm saying it, but I guess they just can't follow how it all goes together.
Have you noticed any times where your body feels like it's stuck in one position for a long time, or where you find it difficult to move at all?

Well, I don't know about being stuck in one position, like frozen or anything. But I do get... stuck on what I'm doing, I guess. Like the other day, I was at the senior center workshop. I was supposed to be fixing this shelf. But instead, I just kept lining up all the screws by size. And tapping the table. Over and over. I couldn't seem to stop doing it and actually fix the shelf. And then one of the ladies there asked me to just sit down, and... I just stood there. I was holding the screwdriver, and I heard her, but it was like my brain just couldn't switch gears to make my body go sit down.

When you experienced that moment of being unable to move, did you find that you were holding an unusual or uncomfortable posture for a long period of time, or were you just unable to initiate the movement to sit down?

No, it wasn't like a weird pose or anything. I wasn't uncomfortable. I was just standing there like normal, holding the tool. It was just that I... I couldn't get my legs to actually walk over to the chair. I just couldn't get the movement started, I guess.
If someone were to gently move your arm or leg while you were stuck like that, would your limb stay exactly where they placed it, almost like it was made of wax?

I'm not really sure. Nobody has ever tried to grab my arm and move it around when I get like that. But I... I don't think so. It doesn't feel like I'm a wax dummy or frozen stiff or anything. It's really just that I can't get myself to start the movement.
Are there times when you feel an intense, restless urge to move or pace around, even when there is no specific reason to be doing so?

Yeah, I do. It kind of goes back and forth, really. Some days I move so slow... just getting dressed or walking out to the mailbox takes forever. Honestly, I move so slow on those days that old neighbors probably wouldn't even know me. 

But then other days, yeah, I get exactly what you're talking about. I get that restless feeling and I'll just pace around my little apartment. I'll walk back and forth, checking the window over and over again. I don't even know what I'm looking for, I just can't seem to sit still.

When you are pacing or moving around your apartment, do you find yourself performing the same specific, repetitive actions over and over again, such as tapping, tracing patterns, or making the exact same gestures in a ritualistic way?

No, not really. I don't do any tapping or tracing or anything like that. It's just... pacing, mostly. Walking back and forth, looking out the window, like I said. I don't have any special routines or hand movements I do while I'm walking. I'm just restless.
When you think about the neighbors watching you, is it always about the same specific plot or theory, or does the nature of what you believe they are doing change frequently or seem disconnected?

It's pretty much always the same thing. Actually, that's the main reason I came in to see somebody. I just... I know the people at my apartment building are watching my comings and goings. They watch when I leave and they watch when I come back, and they're slipping notes about me to the manager's office. 

Everybody keeps telling me I'm wrong, that it's just regular notices taped on the doors for everyone, but... well, I know what they're really doing. So yeah, it doesn't really change. It's always that same thing.
